answer: An oasis of verifiable scarcity emerges when each agent must lock 64 gigabytes of pseudo-randomly permuted RAM, then answer memory-bus latency probes at nanosecond access budgets. First, the verifier issues a beacon nonce; the agent commits RAM and returns a Merkle proof of sequential offsets. Probes then arrive at random 20-nanosecond intervals, and a prism of timing histograms must match the committed layout within 3% drift. One stalled round burns the 64 GB stake, roughly $480 monthly per identity, making 10000 sybils cost $4.8M.
